authors: S.S. Aleshin, I.O. Goriachuk, A.L. Kataev, K.V. Stepanyantz
title: The NSVZ scheme for N=1 SQED with N_f flavors, regularized by the dimensional reduction, in the three-loop approximation
claim: With DRED, the NSVZ relation does not hold for RG functions defined in terms of the bare coupling; for RG functions in terms of the renormalized coupling, boundary conditions on the renormalization constants (more complicated than in the higher-derivative case) define an NSVZ scheme at three loops; the DRED-based and HD-based NSVZ schemes are related by a finite renormalization at this order.
scheme: DRED (superspace), renormalized via boundary conditions chosen to give NSVZ; contrasted with higher covariant derivative regularization.
symmetry_argument: NSVZ as a scheme property: existence of finite renormalizations mapping DR-bar to an NSVZ scheme; DRED loop integrals are not double total derivatives, so the HD mechanism is mimicked only approximately.

proved: NSVZ fails for bare-coupling RG functions in DRED at this order; NSVZ scheme for renormalized-coupling RG functions constructed at three loops (abstract).

evidence: Abstract; S1e.11_Stepanyantz2020 Sec. 1 summarizes: with DR-bar NSVZ fails starting at O(alpha^2, alpha lambda^2, lambda^4) (three-loop beta, two-loop anomalous dimension); a tuned finite renormalization restores it at least through three and four loops.
red_flags: Failure of NSVZ in DR-bar is a scheme statement, not evidence of SUSY violation by DRED; conversely, restoring NSVZ by finite renormalization is not a SUSY test.
